keep.reason: ModelRecognised covers failure cases (binary check error, fail-open) not just successful recognition — the name alone doesn't convey this crucial invariant.
The 5-second timeout is based on measured baseline (~1s) plus slack — the specific value and its rationale are non-obvious.
The verdict is determined by stderr content, never exit code — this is a critical invariant that breaks code if misunderstood.
Cache invalidation on any BinaryIdentity change (path, size, mtime) is non-obvious; reader needs to understand this affects all cached verdicts.
Errors from ResolveBinaryIdentity are treated like unchecked checks, never cached — the contract is non-obvious from the function signature alone.
Multiple non-obvious constraints: determinism, token/port healing via script rewrites, word-split issue with unquoted paths, no HTTP entries written.
The 0o700 mode (not 0o755) is required because the script embeds the ingest token — this security constraint is critical and non-obvious.
Atomicity guarantee (no truncation, readers see consistent state) and the unchanged-content optimization are non-obvious and essential for durability.
The defer cleanup is a no-op once the rename succeeds — worth noting as it guards against misunderstanding the cleanup's purpose.
fsync is required for durability (not just atomicity) before rename; a crash between them can lose the write otherwise.
The ingest URL is stored only inside wrapper scripts, never on the launcher — this architectural constraint is non-obvious.
The nil-means-skip behavior and the unused-dir parameter are subtle implementation details that guard test compatibility.
Two features must resolve the same claude binary default — this consistency invariant is critical and non-obvious.
Single cache owner constraint and that it's always a real modelsFeature in production (tests construct manually) is non-obvious.
Ordering constraint (check before any writes) enables rollback-free refusal; fail-open behavior is critical for fault tolerance.
Shared-repo race on settings.local.json between concurrent sessions launching into the same directory is non-obvious and has serious consequences.
Cache size of 64 is based on measured typical usage (~5 entries) plus headroom; no LRU eviction is sufficient because usage stays well below the limit.
Two verdict types exist because claudecode.ModelVerdict's boundary rule prevents adding 'unchecked' to it; this constraint is non-obvious but critical.
Concurrent lookup deduplication behavior — multiple callers for the same (identity, model) share one run rather than starting separate ones.
Single cache owner, identity-based invalidation (all verdicts dropped on identity change), and generation-tracked reads are all non-obvious and critical.
Directory parameter doesn't affect verdict (catalog is built-in); reader needs to understand this to know what checkDir is actually for.
Injectable seam for testing; constructor-default pattern allows tests to override without modifying production code.
Injectable seam for identity resolution; tests can drive identity changes without filesystem or $PATH access.
Generation field enables detection of stale results from in-flight checks that started under a superseded identity.
Concurrency benefit is non-obvious: four cold checks run in parallel, costing approximately one check's wall time instead of four.
Complex concurrent behavior: request sharing, ctx handling (leader's ctx doesn't affect joiner), fail-open on error/timeout are all non-obvious.
Generation-reset race scenario requires this guard — removing a call that's no longer the current inflight entry would break waiters on newer generations.
Error-handling split between packages: stderr stays in claudecode, error logging here — this boundary is non-obvious but important.
Protocol Contract requires exact message match between POST /api/sessions and GET /api/models — this invariant must not drift.
Separation of concerns (New doesn't start goroutines, Start does) and single-place resolution of defaults are non-obvious and important for lifecycle.
Models cache must be built first and shared with newSessionLauncher — this single-cache requirement is non-obvious.
message field appears iff verdict is 'unrecognized' — this invariant is non-obvious and required by the Protocol Contract.
All-or-nothing parsing rule: one bad element rejects the whole response, same as every other wire list.
Parameter bounds (1 to 8 non-empty models) are from Protocol Contract and non-obvious; caller never violates them but the why is not clear.
modelError element is shared by the whole Model row, not owned by individual controls — this ownership model is non-obvious.
Generation-based staleness detection: responses in flight from closed dialogs are dropped; generation bumps on every open.
forceFocusInvalid parameter has complex focus rules with specific exceptions — its usage is non-obvious and the guard before passing true matters.
Generation guard at request time prevents stale responses from merging into new dialog's verdict store after open.
Custom models not in the four presets require their own verdict request; preset models are covered by the dialog-open request.
Generation must be captured before await to guard against stale refusals landing after dialog cancel-and-reopen.
Error routing distinction: model_unrecognized goes to field-level #model-error; every other error to #launch-error.
Staleness guard ensures write and focus-move are both gated on current generation; neither effect happens for stale responses.
Conditional focus on invalid control only when refusal lands in current dialog; stale refusals move no focus.
Editing text implicitly clears any mark from previous text — reader needs to know this to understand no separate clear branch exists.
Organizational principle: pure decisions live beside their controller caller (features/launch.ts), not in render/ — this pattern is non-obvious.
MODEL_PRESETS is the single source of truth coordinated across launch.ts radio guard and index.html markup.
This is the one testability seam for pure verdict-to-state logic; isolation enables unit testing without dialog or DOM.
Generation invalidation on every dialog open ensures in-flight responses from closed dialogs are dropped whole.
Usage constraint (once per open, never per verdict request) is critical; wrong usage breaks staleness detection.
The 'capture at request, compare at arrival' pattern is subtle and critical for staleness detection across dialog resets.
Type-direction principle: builders define types that pure decisions import downward — this organizational pattern is non-obvious.
Presets are disabled iff unrecognized AND not the current selection — the selection-aware condition is non-obvious.
Accessibility consideration: glyph is aria-hidden so caller needs substring match on text, not exact match.
Edge case analysis: invalidControl returns undefined only if selection names no radio, but this doesn't happen for preset selections (radio set is fixed).
Focus rules have exceptions and constraints: default avoids moving focus off enabled controls; forceFocusInvalid exception only on launch-time refusal.
